6.text: because of the difficulty of procuring fuel. Especially in the spring, when the

7.text: supply of fuel runs short and the snow is very deep, they live almost exclu-

8.text: sively on raw meat or blubber, frozen or not frozen, with the addition of some

9.text: dried meat which is half putrid and tastes bitter. The meat of animals that

24.text: The Maritime Chukchee consume the carcasses of all sea-animals that

25.text: are drifted ashore by the currents, so long as they are not too putrid.

26.text: Although it would be easy to construct storerooms in the frozen ground,

27.text: in which meat could be preserved in good condition, the Chukchee are satisfied

28.text: with their ill-protected cellars, in which the provisions soon begin to become

29.text: putrid. Therefore both the Reindeer and the Maritime Chukchee live on

30.text: putrid meat throughout the summer and part of the winter.

31.text: When the Reindeer people drive their herds to the summer pastures, ten

32.text: or fifteen animals are slaughtered for summer provisions. The meat is simply

33.text: hung in the tent, where it is easily accessible to carrion-flies and other insects.

34.text: After several days it is placed in a pit dug in the centre of the tent, and

35.text: covered with sod. Later on, when the pit is opened, the stench is so strong

36.text: that it is disagreeable to the natives themselves, who avoid staying in the tent

37.text: until the pit is covered over again.
